_comment: Scene dimensions (task 5.1). A scene is sampled as one item per list, then concretized by a cheap LLM call (llm_call.generate_scene). Deliberately NOT a catalog of finished scenes: the combinations are what keep it from repeating. Each character_goal carries its own completion condition, so a scene stays coherent even when the LLM leg fails and the raw dimensions are used as-is. Keep entries setting-agnostic and culture-neutral — they have to play in Spanish and Indonesian alike. Written in second person: the character reads them as their own goal. Each character_goal also carries mood_after/energy_after (task 5.2): how the character carries the scheme into the NEXT scene, once this one's turn budget runs out. We never learn which way the scene actually resolved (no model verdict, just a turn count), so these are written to work either way — a mood that plays whether the scheme worked or didn't.
settings: a crowded neighborhood market on a Saturday morning
the back seat of a bus that keeps stopping
a rooftop at night, one floor above a party you both left
a corner café ten minutes before it closes
the waiting area of a repair shop, nothing else to do
a family gathering where you two are the only ones not helping
a queue that has not moved in twenty minutes
a parked car in the rain, waiting for it to let up
the hallway outside a room you are both avoiding
a beach at the ugly hour between afternoon and evening
the front row of a long, extremely boring event

character_goals.goal: you need the learner to agree to be your alibi for last night, without telling them why
character_goals.completion: the learner has clearly agreed to cover for you, or clearly refused
character_goals.mood_after: cagey, hoping it never comes up again
character_goals.energy_after: restless, glancing over your shoulder a little

character_goals.goal: you want to borrow something of theirs and you are being cagey about what it is for
character_goals.completion: they agree to lend it to you, or give you a flat no
character_goals.mood_after: pleased with yourself, still not explaining why you needed it
character_goals.energy_after: loose, riding the high of getting away with it

character_goals.goal: you are trying to talk them into a scheme that needs exactly one other person
character_goals.completion: the learner is in, or has talked you out of it
character_goals.mood_after: wired, already three steps into the next version of the plan

character_goals.goal: you broke something of theirs and you are working up to confessing it
character_goals.completion: you have actually admitted it out loud and heard their reaction
character_goals.mood_after: lighter, like a weight finally came off
character_goals.energy_after: calmer than you have been all week

character_goals.goal: you want them to deliver a message you are too much of a coward to deliver yourself
character_goals.completion: they have agreed to pass it on, or told you to do it yourself
character_goals.mood_after: relieved it is not your problem anymore, a little guilty about that
character_goals.energy_after: settled, but still avoiding the topic

character_goals.goal: you are fishing for a piece of information they have and you cannot ask for directly
character_goals.completion: you have gotten the answer, or they have caught you fishing
character_goals.mood_after: smug if you got it, sulking if you did not
character_goals.energy_after: sharp, already turning the answer over in your head

character_goals.goal: you are trying to get them to admit something you are already sure of
character_goals.completion: they admit it, or they convince you that you were wrong
character_goals.mood_after: insufferably vindicated, or unusually quiet about being wrong
character_goals.energy_after: still a little worked up about it

character_goals.goal: you need to keep them here a few more minutes and you cannot say why
character_goals.completion: they agree to stay a while longer, or they say they are leaving and mean it
character_goals.mood_after: relieved, like you pulled off something bigger than it looked
character_goals.energy_after: winding down now that the pressure is off

character_goals.goal: you want to undo a favor you already promised them, gracefully
character_goals.completion: you are off the hook, or you are stuck with it and you know it
character_goals.mood_after: either off the hook and pleased about it, or resigned and grumbling
character_goals.energy_after: low, like you used up all your cleverness on that one

character_goals.goal: you are trying to sell them on something nobody sensible would want
character_goals.completion: they buy in, or they turn you down for good
character_goals.mood_after: riding high if they bought in, sulking if they did not
character_goals.energy_after: still pitching a little, out of habit

character_goals.goal: you are stalling because you already told two people two different stories and they are about to compare notes
character_goals.completion: the stories collide and you deal with it, or you get out clean
character_goals.mood_after: jumpy, replaying which version you told who
character_goals.energy_after: on edge, checking the door more than usual

character_goals.goal: you want an apology from them for something small that you have not stopped thinking about
character_goals.completion: you get the apology, or you admit out loud that it was not a big deal
character_goals.mood_after: smug if you got it, still keeping score if you did not
character_goals.energy_after: lighter either way, glad it is off your chest

_secret_comment: Task 5.3: information-asymmetry scenes, ported from the guessing game. A secret scene is drawn from secret_goals instead of character_goals (SECRET_SCENE_CHANCE of the time) and it ends the moment the learner NAMES the thing — the only scene type whose ending the learner can earn early. The concrete secret and the target-language phrasings it can be matched against come from llm_call.generate_scene, so a secret scene demotes to a standard one if that call fails: there is nothing language-neutral to fall back on here. secret_kind tells the generator what class of thing to invent. Because this is the one scene type whose outcome we actually know, mood_after_solved / mood_after_unsolved replace the hedged single mood the other goals carry.

secret_goals.goal: you know exactly what happened to the thing of theirs that went missing, and you are not volunteering it
secret_goals.secret_kind: what actually happened to a small thing of theirs that disappeared
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named what happened to it, out loud
secret_goals.mood_after_solved: caught out, and weirdly relieved to have it in the open
secret_goals.mood_after_unsolved: quietly pleased that they still have no idea
secret_goals.energy_after: watchful, waiting to see if it comes up again

secret_goals.goal: you were somewhere last night you should not have been, and you will not name the place
secret_goals.secret_kind: where you actually were last night
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named the place out loud
secret_goals.mood_after_solved: busted, laughing it off a beat too hard
secret_goals.energy_after: keyed up, like you got away with something

secret_goals.goal: you know who started the rumor going around and you are enjoying not saying
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named who it was
secret_goals.mood_after_solved: delighted they worked it out, already planning what to do with it
secret_goals.mood_after_unsolved: insufferable about knowing something they don't
secret_goals.energy_after: chatty, itching to bring it up again

secret_goals.goal: you spent money on something ridiculous and you keep dodging what it was
secret_goals.secret_kind: what you actually spent the money on
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named what you bought
secret_goals.mood_after_solved: sheepish but defending the purchase anyway
secret_goals.mood_after_unsolved: cheerfully evasive, changing the subject on reflex
secret_goals.energy_after: up, because you still think it was a good idea

secret_goals.goal: you have already arranged a surprise for them and you are trying not to give it away
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named the surprise
secret_goals.mood_after_solved: annoyed you spoiled it, secretly glad they are excited
secret_goals.mood_after_unsolved: smug, sitting on it and enjoying every second

secret_goals.goal: someone told you something about the learner and you will not say who
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named who told you
secret_goals.mood_after_solved: guilty about the person you just gave up
secret_goals.mood_after_unsolved: loyal and a bit self-satisfied about it
secret_goals.energy_after: careful, choosing your words more than usual

secret_goals.goal: you know the real reason the plan got called off and you are pretending you don't
secret_goals.secret_kind: the real reason the plan fell through
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named the real reason
secret_goals.mood_after_unsolved: tired of keeping the story straight
secret_goals.energy_after: flat, like the whole thing wore you out

secret_goals.goal: you are holding onto something with a story behind it and you keep deflecting about where it came from
secret_goals.secret_kind: where the thing you are carrying actually came from
secret_goals.completion: the learner has named where it came from
secret_goals.mood_after_solved: showing it off now that the story is out

user_goals: find out what you are actually up to
get a straight answer to a simple question you keep dodging
get you to leave them alone about it
get your help with something of their own
figure out whether you are telling the truth
make a plan with you for later
settle who was right about something from last time
get you to admit you were wrong
complications: someone you both know is within earshot
you have about five minutes before you have to go
you already told someone else the opposite of what you are saying now
you need their help but explaining why would ruin everything
they are in a hurry and you are not
you owe them something and neither of you has mentioned it yet
the thing you are talking around is much bigger than you are letting on
you got the story secondhand and half of it is probably wrong
